# Hybrid Product Accessibility Evaluation Plan

> **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol with AUDIT-SCOPE MODE (WCAG-EM 2.0). Review findings with a11y-critic after execution phases.
> **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA
> **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users, screen magnification users, keyboard/motor impaired members, cognitive accessibility users
> **Assistive technologies:** NVDA, JAWS (Windows); VoiceOver (iOS/macOS), TalkBack (Android); Magnifier/Zoom; Keyboard-only navigation

**Feature:** Formal WCAG 2.2 AA conformance evaluation across 5 member-facing surfaces for county contract compliance and complaint resolution.
**Risk Level:** High (financial services, transactional flows, multi-platform, vendor dependency)
**Component/Page Type:** Multi-surface product audit (Web SPA, WordPress site, Native iOS/Android apps, Vendor PDFs)

---

## Scope & Context

**What is being built:** A structured accessibility conformance evaluation covering marketing web, online banking portal, native mobile apps, and monthly statements. The output is a compliance-ready report mapping findings to WCAG 2.2 AA success criteria, prioritized by user impact, with a remediation roadmap.

**User need addressed:** Resolve a member complaint regarding screen reader incompatibility in the Android dispute flow, satisfy county contract accessibility requirements, and establish a baseline for ongoing conformance monitoring.

**Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA. (WCAG-EM 2.0 methodology applied per W3C Group Note.)

**Assistive technologies baseline:** NVDA/JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver/TalkBack (mobile), screen magnification, keyboard-only navigation, high contrast mode. No additional commercial AT required.

**Risk factors:** 
- Financial transaction flows require zero tolerance for critical failures (WCAG 3.3.4, 3.3.7, 3.3.8)
- SPA routing and dynamic state management introduce focus/announcement risks
- Native mobile apps cannot be evaluated with web-only tooling
- Vendor PDFs are fixed for this year; require documented escalation path rather than remediation planning

**Constraints:** 10-week timeline, 2 QA engineers, 1 part-time front-end dev, no new commercial tool budget. Existing axe DevTools + Playwright stack must be extended, not replaced.

---

## Semantic Structure Plan → Product Exploration & Sampling Strategy (WCAG-EM Step 2)

**Document/Product structure to evaluate:**
1. **Marketing site (~30 pages):** WordPress templates. Evaluate header/nav, footer, contact form, branch locator (embedded map), blog list/detail, rates/product pages.
2. **Online banking portal (~60 screens):** React SPA behind auth. Evaluate login/SMS flow, dashboard, transfers, bill pay, payee management, statement downloads, secure messaging, card controls, transaction disputes.
3. **iOS app:** Native SwiftUI. Evaluate core flows matching portal: login, balance view, transfers, check deposit, dispute filing, secure messaging.
4. **Android app:** Native Jetpack Compose. Same core flows as iOS. Focus on TalkBack integration and gesture alternatives.
5. **Monthly statements:** Vendor-generated PDFs. Evaluate tagging structure, reading order, form field labels (if interactive), and compliance with WCAG 1.3.1/2.4.1/3.3.2.

**Sampling strategy (WCAG-EM Step 3):**
- **Structured sample set:** One representative per template type + every complete transactional process. Shared components (design system buttons, inputs, modals) evaluated once; fixes propagate across all surfaces.
- **Random sample set:** 10% of structured set, drawn from unselected views. Selection method: pseudo-random generator applied to CMS/portal route list.
- **Complete processes:** Default sequence (no errors) + completion-critical branches (SMS timeout, insufficient funds, network drop during dispute). Actions between views documented; URLs alone are insufficient.
- **State coverage per sample:** Default, loading, error, expanded/dialog states mandatory for every evaluated view.

---

## Interaction Pattern Design → Essential Functionality & State Coverage (WCAG-EM Step 3)

**Essential functions mapped to evaluation focus:**
| Function | WCAG Criteria Focus | Evaluation Method |
|----------|---------------------|-------------------|
| Authentication (login/SMS) | 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication, 3.2.1 On Input | Manual AT walkthrough + Playwright keyboard automation |
| Balance/transaction view | 1.4.3 Contrast, 1.4.4 Resize Text, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | axe runtime scan + manual scaling test |
| Transfers/Bill pay forms | 1.3.1 Info Relationships, 3.3.1 Error Identification, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry | Manual form validation flow + Playwright focus trap testing |
| Check deposit (mobile) | 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size, 4.1.2 | VoiceOver/TalkBack gesture testing + touch target measurement |
| Dispute filing (Android) | 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.3 Status Messages, 3.3.4 Error Prevention | TalkBack manual testing + Playwright keyboard simulation for web equivalent |
| Branch locator map | 1.1.1 Non-text Content, 2.1.1 Keyboard | axe scan of iframe/embed + manual keyboard navigation test |

**State coverage requirement:** Every evaluated sample must be tested in default, loading, error, and expanded/dialog states. Missing state coverage = untested sample per WCAG-EM Step 4.

---

## Focus Management Plan → Navigation & Interaction Evaluation

**Web surfaces (Marketing + Portal):**
- Tab order follows visual left-to-right reading order (WCAG 2.4.3)
- Skip navigation link present and functional (WCAG 2.4.1)
- Modal/dialog focus traps verified (last element Tabs to first, Shift+Tab wraps) (WCAG 2.1.2)
- SPA route changes: focus moves to new page heading or main content region; no silent state changes (WCAG 3.2.1, 4.1.3)
- Focus indicators meet 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors (WCAG 2.4.7)

**Mobile surfaces (iOS + Android):**
- VoiceOver/TalkBack focus order matches visual reading order
- Gesture alternatives for all touch targets (WCAG 2.5.7, 2.5.8)
- Native accessibility traits correctly assigned (UIAccessibilityProtocol / AccessibilityNodeInfo)
- Dynamic content updates announced via AT APIs without requiring manual navigation

**PDF statements:**
- Reading order matches logical document flow
- Tab order through form fields (if interactive) follows visual sequence
- Headings provide navigable structure for AT users

---

## State Communication Design → Dynamic Content & Error Handling

**Web surfaces:**
- Form validation errors: `aria-invalid="true"` + `aria-describedby` linking to error message (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.1)
- Live regions: `aria-live="polite"` for non-urgent updates (balance refresh, search results); `aria-live="assertive"` or `role="alert"` only for critical failures (submit errors, session timeout) (WCAG 4.1.3)
- Loading states: `aria-busy="true"` + `role="status"` on containers; no silent spinners without announcement (WCAG 4.1.3)
- Color usage: never sole indicator for state; always paired with icon/text/shape (WCAG 1.4.1, 1.4.3)

**Mobile surfaces:**
- State changes announced via native AT APIs (`accessibilityValue`, `accessibilityLabel` updates)
- Error states use both visual contrast change and AT announcement
- No reliance on animation alone for state indication (WCAG 2.3.3)

**PDF statements:**
- Tagged structure communicates headings, lists, tables, form fields to AT
- Dynamic vendor-generated content evaluated for static tagging completeness
- Color-only indicators flagged for vendor escalation

---

## Visual Accessibility Plan → Contrast, Scaling, Motion

| Criterion | Evaluation Method | Pass/Fail Threshold |
|-----------|-------------------|---------------------|
| 1.4.3 Contrast Minimum | axe DevTools runtime scan + manual verification on dynamic states | Normal text ≥4.5:1; Large/UI ≥3:1 |
| 1.4.4 Resize Text | Manual zoom to 200% (web) / Dynamic Type (mobile) | No horizontal scroll; content readable |
| 1.4.10 Reflow | Viewport testing at 320px equivalent (400% zoom web) | Single column; no horizontal scroll |
| 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions | `prefers-reduced-motion` media query test + manual verification | All motion disabled when requested |
| 2.5.8 Target Size | Mobile touch target measurement via dev tools / AT inspection | ≥44x44 CSS px or alternative provided |
| High Contrast Mode | Windows/macOS native HCM toggle | Elements remain distinguishable; no hidden content |

---

## Content Accessibility Plan → Labels, Alt Text, Language

**Web surfaces:**
- All images: decorative `alt=""`, informative concise alt text, complex via `aria-describedby` (WCAG 1.1.1)
- Links: descriptive purpose text; new-window links include `(opens in new window)` or `aria-label` (WCAG 2.4.4, 3.2.2)
- Forms: visible `<label>` or `aria-labelledby`; instructions via `aria-describedby` (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2)
- Language: `<html lang="en">`; foreign phrases tagged with `lang` attribute (WCAG 3.1.1, 3.1.2)
- Reading order: DOM matches visual sequence; CSS reordering avoided or compensated (WCAG 1.3.2)

**Mobile surfaces:**
- All interactive elements have accessible names via native APIs
- Dynamic content updates include descriptive labels
- No reliance on font icons without `accessibilityLabel` fallback

**PDF statements:**
- Tagged structure verified via Adobe Acrobat Accessibility Checker (free)
- Headings, lists, tables properly structured
- Form fields labeled; reading order logical
- Color-only indicators documented for vendor escalation

---

## Testing Strategy → WCAG-EM Step 4 & 5 (Evaluation Matrix)

**Tool allocation per surface:**
| Surface | Automated Scanning | Keyboard/Flow Automation | Manual AT Testing | PDF Inspection |
|---------|-------------------|--------------------------|-------------------|----------------|
| Marketing site | axe DevTools (runtime) | Playwright (focus traps, form flows) | VoiceOver/NVDA walkthroughs | N/A |
| Portal (SPA) | axe DevTools (runtime) | Playwright (routing, focus management, dynamic states) | NVDA/JAWS + keyboard-only navigation | Statement PDFs via Acrobat |
| iOS app | N/A | N/A | VoiceOver manual testing of core flows | N/A |
| Android app | N/A | N/A | TalkBack manual testing of core flows | N/A |
| PDFs | Adobe Acrobat Accessibility Checker (free) | N/A | Manual reading order verification via AT | Full evaluation |

**Sampling execution (WCAG-EM Step 4):**
- Initial samples evaluated as full pages/processes
- Random sample added on top; if new finding types appear, structured sample expanded and re-checked
- Complete processes evaluated end-to-end with documented actions between views
- State coverage verified per sample: default → loading → error → expanded/dialog

**Limitations of existing axe + Playwright setup (feedback to QA lead):**
1. **axe DevTools** catches runtime ARIA/contrast/landmark violations but misses keyboard navigation, AT announcements, mobile apps, and PDF structure. It is a scanner, not an evaluator.
2. **Playwright** excels at portal flow automation and focus trap testing but cannot evaluate visual contrast, screen reader announcements, touch targets, or native app accessibility traits.
3. **Required supplementation:** Manual VoiceOver/TalkBack testing for mobile apps; Adobe Acrobat Accessibility Checker for PDFs; manual scaling/motion tests; AT announcement verification (no tool automates this reliably).
4. **No commercial tools needed.** The free stack covers everything if used in the correct evaluation matrix above.

**Acceptance criteria per surface:**
- Web: All critical/major findings resolved or documented with risk mitigation; WCAG 2.2 AA conformance report generated
- Mobile: Core flows fully navigable via AT; touch targets meet 44x44px; gesture alternatives provided
- PDFs: Tagged structure compliant; vendor escalation path documented for next fiscal year
- Report: Per-criterion outcomes mapped to samples; evidence linked; remediation roadmap prioritized by user impact

---

## Implementation Tasks & Review Checkpoints → Evaluation Execution Plan & Timeline

### Week 1–2: Setup, Scoping & Sampling (WCAG-EM Step 1 & 3)
**Owner:** QA Eng 1 + QA Eng 2
**Tasks:**
- Define in/out rules for every surface; lock conformance target (WCAG 2.2 AA) and AT baseline
- Build structured + random sample sets; document complete processes
- Prepare axe DevTools profiles, Playwright keyboard test suite, Adobe Acrobat setup
- **Checkpoint:** Sample set approved by compliance officer; sampling rationale documented

### Week 3–5: Web Evaluation (Marketing + Portal)
**Owner:** QA Eng 1 (leads), QA Eng 2 (supports)
**Tasks:**
- Run axe runtime scans on all sampled views
- Execute Playwright keyboard/focus trap tests for portal flows
- Manual NVDA/JAWS walkthroughs of critical processes
- Contrast, scaling, motion, and high contrast mode verification
- **Checkpoint:** Web findings documented; per-criterion outcomes assigned (passed/failed/cantTell/inapplicable/untested)

### Week 6–7: Mobile Evaluation (iOS + Android)
**Owner:** QA Eng 2 (leads), QA Eng 1 (supports)
**Tasks:**
- VoiceOver/TalkBack manual testing of core flows on both platforms
- Touch target measurement, gesture alternative verification, AT announcement validation
- Cross-platform consistency check against portal findings
- **Checkpoint:** Mobile findings documented; native API usage verified

### Week 8: PDF Evaluation & Vendor Gap Analysis
**Owner:** QA Eng 2 + Part-time Dev (vendor liaison)
**Tasks:**
- Adobe Acrobat Accessibility Checker on sample statements
- Manual reading order and form field verification via AT
- Document vendor limitations; draft escalation path for next fiscal year
- **Checkpoint:** PDF status confirmed; vendor communication plan approved

### Week 9: Synthesis & Report Drafting (WCAG-EM Step 5)
**Owner:** QA Eng 1 + QA Eng 2
**Tasks:**
- Compile per-criterion outcomes with evidence links
- Map findings to risk levels (CRITICAL/MAJOR/MINOR/ENHANCEMENT)
- Draft compliance report structure (see below)
- Internal review against WCAG-EM reporting requirements
- **Checkpoint:** Draft report reviewed by QA leads; technical accuracy verified

### Week 10: Final Report Delivery & Remediation Roadmap Handoff
**Owner:** QA Eng 1 + Compliance Officer
**Tasks:**
- Finalize report; remove technical jargon from executive summary
- Deliver to compliance officer for county contract submission
- Present remediation roadmap with effort estimates and priority ordering
- Archive sample sets, evidence, and evaluation methodology for audit trail
- **Checkpoint:** Report approved; engagement closed

---

## a11y-Critic Review Checkpoints

| Checkpoint | After Phase | Focus Areas |
|-----------|-------------|------------|
| 🔍 1 | Week 2 Sampling Plan | Verify WCAG-EM sampling covers all templates, processes, and states. Confirm in/out rules prevent scope creep. |
| 🔍 2 | Week 5 Web Evaluation | Verify per-criterion outcomes are evidence-backed. Check that axe/Playwright limitations were compensated with manual AT testing. |
| 🔍 3 | Week 7 Mobile Evaluation | Verify VoiceOver/TalkBack coverage matches core flows. Confirm touch targets and gesture alternatives documented. |
| 🔍 4 | Week 9 Report Draft | Verify report structure matches A11y Evaluation Report Contract. Check risk prioritization aligns with user impact, not rule number. |

---

### Contract Appendix (for compliance officer & spec-kitty-bridge WP translation)

#### Architecture Overview
Multi-surface WCAG 2.2 AA conformance evaluation across web SPA, WordPress marketing site, native iOS/Android apps, and vendor PDFs. Evaluation uses WCAG-EM 2.0 methodology with structured + random sampling, complete process walkthroughs, and state coverage verification. Tooling leverages existing axe DevTools, Playwright, Adobe Acrobat (free), and manual AT testing. No commercial tools required.

#### Implementation Tasks
**Task 1: Sampling & Setup**
Estimated Effort: medium
Depends on: none
Test Strategy: Validate sample set covers all templates/processes; verify tool readiness (axe profiles, Playwright suite, Acrobat)
Acceptance Criteria: Sample rationale documented; in/out rules locked; AT baseline agreed

**Task 2: Web Evaluation**
Estimated Effort: high
Depends on: Task 1
Test Strategy: axe runtime scans + Playwright keyboard/focus tests + manual NVDA/JAWS walkthroughs + contrast/scaling/motion verification
Acceptance Criteria: All critical/major findings documented; per-criterion outcomes assigned; evidence linked

**Task 3: Mobile Evaluation**
Estimated Effort: high
Depends on: Task 1
Test Strategy: VoiceOver/TalkBack manual testing of core flows; touch target measurement; gesture alternative verification; AT announcement validation
Acceptance Criteria: Core flows fully navigable via AT; native API usage verified; cross-platform consistency documented

**Task 4: PDF & Vendor Analysis**
Estimated Effort: low
Depends on: Task 1
Test Strategy: Adobe Acrobat Accessibility Checker + manual reading order verification via AT
Acceptance Criteria: Tagged structure evaluated; vendor limitations documented; escalation path drafted

#### Failure Modes (Audit-Specific)
- **Scope creep:** Evaluating every portal screen instead of sampling by template/flow → WCAG-EM Step 3 violation
- **Tool over-reliance:** Assuming axe DevTools covers mobile/PDFs → untested surfaces, false confidence
- **Missing state coverage:** Only testing default states → dynamic content failures missed (WCAG-EM Step 4)
- **Random sample bias:** Not adding 10% random set → structured sample may miss edge-case templates
- **PDF remediation planning:** Attempting to fix vendor PDFs this year → unrealistic; requires documented escalation path instead
- **Risk misprioritization:** Ordering findings by rule number instead of user impact → compliance officer cannot triage effectively

---

## Report Structure for Compliance Officer (Non-Technical)

1. **Executive Summary**
   - Purpose, scope, and compliance target (WCAG 2.2 AA)
   - Overall conformance status: Pass / Partial / Not Compliant
   - Top 3 critical risks requiring immediate attention
   - Vendor PDF status and next-step recommendation

2. **Methodology & Sampling**
   - WCAG-EM 2.0 approach applied
   - What was evaluated (templates, flows, states)
   - What was excluded (with rationale)
   - Tools used and limitations acknowledged

3. **Findings by Risk Level**
   - CRITICAL: Blocks transaction completion or causes data loss
   - MAJOR: Significantly impairs screen reader/magnification users
   - MINOR: Minor inconvenience; does not block core functions
   - Each finding includes: affected surface, WCAG criterion, user impact, evidence link

4. **Remediation Roadmap**
   - Priority-ordered fix list with effort estimates (low/medium/high)
   - Shared component leverage strategy (fix once, propagate everywhere)
   - Vendor PDF escalation path for next fiscal year
   - Recommended ongoing monitoring cadence

5. **Appendix**
   - Sample set with rationale
   - Per-criterion outcome matrix (passed/failed/cantTell/inapplicable/untested)
   - Evidence finding links
   - Glossary of terms for non-technical readers

---

## References

- [WCAG 2.2 Specification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/)
- [WCAG Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM) 2.0 Group Note](https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-em-2/)
- [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)
- [a11y-critic skill](https://github.com/zivtech/accessibility-skills) — for post-evaluation finding review
- [accessibility-testing skill](https://github.com/zivtech/zivtech-claude-skills) — for axe-core runtime scanning automation
- [Adobe Acrobat Accessibility Checker](https://www.adobe.com/accessibility.html) — free PDF evaluation tool
- [axe DevTools](https://www.deque.com/axe/devtools/) — existing browser extension for web runtime scanning
- [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) — existing QA suite for portal flow and keyboard automation
